, including mixture composition, atmosphere, and illumination
history for each measurement block.","If the optional bridge is used, the same classes of

directionality in optional P02 would strengthen plausibility that donor
-side behavior contributes, but would still not establish causation or a
shared mechanism.","refutes":"H02 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give similar donor-side

management, catalyst-state, substrate-binding, or other donor-induced changes not captured by the
selected photophysical observables.","inconclusive":"The result is inconclusive
if TEA and TEOA formulations cannot be matched reproducibly, if photophysical signals are below assignment confidence
or dominated by scattering or support artifacts, if sample-state linkage between phot
ophysics and catalysis is not demonstrated, if background product formation is
too large to isolate cobalt-dependent behavior, or if multiple observables shift in inconsistent directions.","parameter
_selection":"Do not invent donor concentration, catalyst loading, light intensity, or sampling times. Start from
the literature-anchored P01 baseline formulation and verify exact values from the supplied system recommendation. Before the full comparison, run
a pilot to choose a dilution window that keeps optical signals measurable without changing component identities, confirms linear detector response, and avoids complete
inner-filter saturation. Choose catalytic sampling times by bracketing early,
mid, and later illumination intervals where both CO and H2 are above detection and cobalt-omission controls remain
interpretable. For each measurement block, first confirm that the defined pre-measurement history yields
stable backgrounds and comparable spectra
in duplicate preparations. For
the optional P02 bridge, first confirm observable quenching in the
TEOA formulation before introducing TEA as the single-variable comparator.","limitations":"This design tests correlation versus discordance, not
causation. Even reproducible concordance between donor-side observables and CO/H2
does not exclude coupled changes in proton transfer, catalyst speciation, substrate binding
, or other downstream chemistry. P01 support effects may decouple measured optical observables from the chemically active manifold.
Cobalt-omission contrasts are necessity/background tests because omitting cobalt changes the reaction manifold
. The optional P02 bridge improves photophysical interpretability but is not chemically identical to the Co
-bpy/g-C3N4 target, so only bounded directionality transfer is justified.","feasibility":"moderate"}
